rules: HTTPS certificate verification required; fixed origin/endpoints, no client-supplied URL and no credential-bearing redirect following.
Cache-Control: no-store; Referrer-Policy: no-referrer on all pairing replies/pages. No third-party assets on verification/consent page.
Never put device codes/account keys in URLs, browser JSON/HTML/storage, postMessage, logs or exception text. Only start/status backend responses may carry the stated secrets.
No permissive CORS/browser token exchange. Reject malformed/extra credential fields, duplicate parameters, arrays for scalars and unsupported client IDs.
Do not treat public client_id, installation_id or display label as verified software/domain identity.

start.auth: Anonymous backend request, issuance limits mandatory; not account authorization.

response.user_code: <two base32 slot characters + eight random base32 characters, displayed XX-XXXX-XXXX>

notes: Create only a pending record; no account key or user is looked up.
Do not accept redirect_uri, callback, arbitrary scope, account_id or requested credential type.

status.auth: Authorization: Bearer <device_code>; never cookie authentication as substitute.
notes: For cryptolabs-dc-controller service_intent is watchdog; Overview alerts are not enabled. service_intent is metadata, not an enforceable key scope.
Return only these fields. Never return JWT/admin flags, provider SSO/signing keys, litellm_api_key, dc_overview_instances or serialized validation/account objects.
The account id/email derive from approved WP user and current server data; never caller fields. Recheck user existence/email verification before delivery.
A valid identity/key is not a new paid entitlement. Current service validation remains authoritative.

consent_surface.behavior: Render fixed verification surface; require login for code lookup/consent. GET never approves, denies or redeems. Login return is the fixed same-origin surface with no secret/code query. User enters visible code; existing signup pages open separately without a deployment callback. After signup/verification, return to surface and re-enter code; expired attempt restarts from local app.
consent_surface.lookup: Nonce-protected same-origin POST to fixed surface, action=review, user_code. Match full code HMAC, not slot alone. Show escaped unverified installation label, canonical product, chosen account, exact matching code and account-wide credential warning.

approve.auth: Current logged-in WP cookie + valid wp_rest nonce + independent consent nonce bound to full user-code digest and current WP user. No anonymous or application-password consent.
notes: decision is approve or deny; deny returns status denied and terminalizes attempt.
Only pending -> approved/denied CAS. Reject missing/invalid nonce, user mismatch, unverified email, unknown code, expiration or prior decision. GET and account signup cannot approve.
Ensure existing product credential can be reused through existing issuer; no rotation, trial start, subscription mutation or account creation from this endpoint.
A logged-in user who enters an unsolicited attacker code can still approve attacker hardware: show explicit context; not phishing resistant.

invalid_grant.meaning: Unknown/mismatched code/client/secret, already consumed or superseded slot; generic no account disclosure.

expired_token.meaning: Matched legitimate attempt expired; no credential.

authorization_pending.meaning: Valid backend request, not yet approved.

slow_down.meaning: Poll too early; increase interval by 5 seconds for remaining attempt; atomic next_poll update.

email_verification_required.meaning: Use existing verification flow; no email policy bypass.

account_setup_required.meaning: Existing issuer/provisioning cannot supply supported credential; direct user to existing signup/account page, no arbitrary creation policy.

temporarily_unavailable.meaning: Persistence/query/issuer failure or exhausted CAS; preserve old link, never deliver credential on uncertain consumption.

rate_limited.meaning: Retry-After provided; capacity or rate limiter exhausted.

storage.table: Existing wp_options only; no new runtime file/table/billing migration.

value.expires_at: integer UTC epoch from DB time
value.user_code_digest: HMAC-SHA256(full normalized user code, domain-separated wp_salt('auth'))

storage.reads: Read private namespace with prepared direct SQL every time. Never get_option/get_transient/object cache for attempt or limiter authority. No secrets in these rows. Domain-separated existing WP salt, no new external secret store.
storage.allocation: Choose random slot; INSERT IGNORE nonautoload if absent, otherwise select expired row and atomically replace with exact-old-value CAS. Retry at most32 slots, then429. Reject full normalized code on digest mismatch even if same slot. Old device secrets cannot redeem a reused slot.
storage.cas_sql: UPDATE <wpdb options> SET option_value=%s WHERE option_name=%s AND BINARY option_value=BINARY %s
storage.expiry: Every approval/poll/consume CAS additionally checks captured expires_at > database UNIX_TIMESTAMP(); allocation replacement checks captured expiry <= DB time. Never extend 300s TTL on review/login/poll.
storage.transition: pending->approved/denied; approved->consumed; pending->pending only to update poll timing. Full exact-value CAS plus revision prevents concurrent overwrite; affected_rows must equal1. No successful replay after consumed. Never read-then-delete via transients.
storage.delivery: Resolve/validate existing credential and user server-side, then win approved->consumed CAS immediately before constructing secret response. Only winner may output. Lost response/crash after consume yields no replay: restart new pairing. Database errors/reconnect-uncertain results fail closed; never infer success from a reread of consumed.
storage.cleanup: Fixed512 slots cap pending+terminal storage. Reuse expired slots by CAS; optional bounded32-row expiry cleanup never deletes a changed/live row. No full-table scan or unbounded request-time cleanup.
storage.limiter: Fixed nonautoload rows with same direct SQL CAS, keyed by route + bucket slot. Global minute bucket per route;256 hashed caller buckets per route keep cardinality fixed. Use only REMOTE_ADDR (no X-Forwarded-For/CF headers) for anonymous start/status; authenticated WP user ID for approval. HMAC caller then map to256; collisions share a limit (safe false throttling). DB epoch minute resets count via CAS; 3 retries then503. Start global60/min and caller6/min; status global600/min and caller120/min plus per-attempt 5s; consent/review global300/min and caller30/min. Salt-derived hashing hides addresses. Reverse-proxy peers may share quota: no runtime trust-header change in this increment.
storage.dependencies: WordPress options unique option_name index and atomic single-statement SQL semantics. Real MariaDB multi-connection test must prove CAS, expiration, allocation and limiter limits. No transaction session/GET_LOCK dependency.

reuse: get_or_create_ipmi_api_key($user_id) for existing legacy credential semantics
credential_source.narrow_fix: clai_get_account() delegates to CLAI_Database::get_account() and returns an object, while existing helper indexes an array. Normalize object/array only in existing key lookup, handle absent api_key safely, and test existing meta key, null, object and array paths. Never reinterpret encrypted litellm_key as api_key.
credential_source.issuance: Prefer existing clai_ipmi_api_key. Ordinary signup already provisions it. Existing helper may issue its normal first key if absent; preserve that behavior only. Never call generate_api_key (rotation), start trial or payment handlers from pairing. Do not add a new credential type/lifetime/refresh policy.
credential_source.account_key_limit: Current key is account-wide and shared across products. Visible consent must say so. Local disconnect clears local link only, not central/per-install revocation.

local_adapter.authentication: All local endpoints require current live administrator and existing CSRF/origin protections. Do not accept proxy/client supplied admin identity without existing verified trust boundary.
local_adapter.start: Create backend-persisted random local attempt_id; bind initiating local user, hash of session binding, installation_id, client_id, monotonic generation/current local configuration fingerprint and expiry <=central300s. Keep device secret only in protected server storage; never Flask signed cookie. Browser receives attempt_id,user_code,verification_uri,expires_in,interval only. Start/new attempt supersedes old local attempt atomically.
local_adapter.status: Browser sends attempt_id only; backend reads binding and checks current user/session/admin/expiry then polls central service. Browser cannot send device_code,api_key,account identity or service URL. One local worker claims poll operation by CAS before network; completion CAS must recheck original generation/session/config. Cancel/logout/supersede wins over any late response.
local_adapter.staging: Central success becomes protected backend stage after validation; browser receives only account id/email/display_name, service availability and requires_confirmation. Preserve old credentials/config until explicit local commit for replacement. Clear staged secrets on expiry/cancel/session loss.
local_adapter.commit: Browser POST attempt_id + confirm=true only. Recheck live admin/session, exact attempt generation, unchanged current link/config fingerprint, expiry and staged validation; atomic one-use local transition+configuration transaction. If filesystem-based proxy storage cannot transact multiple files, serialize existing atomic writer with compare-current-state and failure-safe replacement; test crashes and concurrent cancel/commit. No key/browser account hints accepted.
local_adapter.cancel: CAS terminalize current bound local attempt; wipe pending/staged secret; preserve saved valid link. Central attempt expires naturally; no new revoke semantics.
local_adapter.success: Show connected account identity, not passwordless local login; preserve sync choices and worker tokens. Initial successful enablement follows existing explicitly approved product setting semantics; do not silently re-enable disabled sync.
local_adapter.csrf: GET /api/account-link/config requires current live administrator and returns only {csrf_token:<32 random bytes base64url>}, Cache-Control:no-store. Reuse per-session pair_csrf; rotate on session/login identity reset. It may live in the existing signed session cookie because it is a browser CSRF nonce, not a device/account credential. Every local POST requires X-CSRF-Token with constant-time match. If Origin is present it must exactly match the accepted local serving origin including scheme/port; reject Sec-Fetch-Site:cross-site and disallow cross-origin config reads/CORS. Missing Origin does not bypass the mandatory CSRF token. config creates no attempt and returns no device/account key. Existing proxy protections may back this exact API.

browser_contract.blocked_replacement: Same staged response but can_commit=false with reason=service_validation_failed when replacing an existing different credential that the new candidate cannot validate; previous configuration retained.

staged_validation.all: The fixed-origin verified-TLS central redemption is the authoritative account/key binding. Strictly validate exact schema/client/installation, positive integer WP account.id, bounded plausible email and supported credential type. These identity fields never come from browser or get overwritten by service hints. A failed/malformed central result cannot stage a link. Never serialize full downstream validation response.
staged_validation.identity: A new unlinked installation may link a strictly verified central identity even when its paid service is unavailable/not entitled. Persist key + trusted WP identity only after local confirmation, with subscription_valid=false and no enabled paid features unless independently validated. Link status and service status are separate. Preserve local sync choices; no background sync is started just because identity linked. Do not fabricate legacy service customer_id: leave it absent/empty until supplied by a valid service reply, using a narrow identity-only persistence helper rather than pretending the legacy validation helper succeeded.
staged_validation.ipmi_service: Keep validate_license_key unchanged for legacy paths. In the new pairing-specific validator, call existing configured TLS AI /api/v1/validate for current service permission. If reply has valid=true and meets every existing tier/max_servers/features/email/customer_id contract except user_id is absent, call fixed WP POST /ipmi/validate with Authorization Bearer candidate key; require valid=true, exact matching positive user_id and normalized email from central exchange. Only then fill missing user_id from this independent WP response and apply current AI service tier/features/quota. Present mismatching or malformed user_id is a failure, not an omission. Any other missing AI field or either validation error means service_status unavailable/not_entitled/unknown, no paid grant. A complete AI identity also must match central WP account.id/email. Never copy litellm_api_key or dc_overview_instances from WP validation.
staged_validation.existing_link: Do not replace an existing different saved credential/configuration with a candidate that fails service validation. Stage trusted identity and indicate can_commit=false; preserve existing paid flags/settings unchanged. For same-key re-link, record identity only with explicit confirmation and preserve existing configuration; do not newly set paid-valid on validation failure. This does not choose a new outage policy: existing ongoing service validation behavior remains.
staged_validation.proxy: Verify central identity/schema and optionally corroborate via existing fixed WP validation; preserve hosted Watchdog entitlement/enrollment authority. Do not infer paid readiness from watchdog_verified; that flag remains link-completion only. Detect explicit WATCHDOG_API_KEY precedence conflicts before commit and return configuration_conflict, retaining environment/files/worker tokens. No customer/worker reparenting.
staged_validation.standalone: IPMI works without proxy. DCO/Watchdog controller uses existing proxy shared credential path where installed; document supported standalone controller adapter availability rather than claiming unimplemented paths work.

test_contract.php_handler: Exercise actual route registration/start/status/review/approve handlers with synthetic WP request/cookie/nonce boundaries. Include emitted page body and exact JSON; no source-string-only proof.
test_contract.persistence: Two independent PHP/mysqli connections/processes execute the real production direct-SQL helpers against disposable MariaDB/InnoDB options table. Barrier concurrent approves, redeems, stale polling vs approval/cancel, slot reuse and rate counters; one secret reply only, no lost state, no over-limit successful reservations. Fault injection after consumed yields no retry secret.
test_contract.clients: Actual Flask handlers/admin/session store and existing credential/config writers. Shared same JSON fixture contract used by all products. Verify session switch/logout/config change after outbound response, stage mismatch, independent WP identity, missing-only-legacy-user_id case, and atomic preservation on every failure.
test_contract.regression: Reuse IPMI auth/settings security, Proxy auth/admin, DCO token preservation/enrollment and package artifact tests. No Watchdog agent token rotation or billing/retention changes.
test_contract.browser: Owner-admin representative local-only deployment, no provider VPN/inbound route: login/new signup, email verification/restart, matching-code consent, local account confirmation, enabled service checks. Live installed validation remains held until actual accepted Fleet/client and central release.

blockers_only: Real options-table SQL/CAS behavior must pass independent database concurrency tests before gate closure; mocked storage alone is insufficient.
An explicit environment key conflict must be resolved through customer-controlled configuration before replacement; detect and preserve rather than mutate implicitly.
Production/Fleet/paid acceptance remains outside source-contract completion.

AI validation missing required fields holds service-ready/paid acceptance only; strictly verified WP identity linking for an unlinked installation remains available without the unrelated backend rollout.

source_basis.note: Source reads are baseline facts only. Builders use their new approved worktrees and bind exact candidate revisions to results.

handler_seams.registration: register_routes() registers pairing_start, pairing_status, pairing_approve; init() registers render_pairing_page on template_redirect for exact clai_pair=1.
handler_seams.persistence: Private production helpers pairing_store_read($slot), pairing_store_cas($slot,$old,$new,$expiry_mode), pairing_store_allocate($record), pairing_rate_allow($route,$caller). Test public handlers with real wpdb connection; reflection may invoke pure/private storage helpers only in SQL boundary tests. No fake atomics in concurrency tests.
